quote.after:
For the absolutely continuous curve conclusion (c), assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) as required by the cited causal-curve calculus and fundamental theorem. The other clauses use the given smooth observer structure, pointwise adapted-chart existence and finite compactness arguments, without these additional curve-calculus premises. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), and put $n=N/\sqrt{-g(N,N)}$. Write $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. In a chart $(U,x)$ put $v^a=dx^a(v)$, $v_s=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and $|v|_{\mathrm e}=(\sum_{a=0}^3(v^a)^2)^{1/2}$.

**(a) Adapted orthonormal charts.** For every $p\in M$ there are a chart $(U,x)$, $x(p)=0$, a radius $r>0$ with $U=x^{-1}(B_r)$, and $K\ge1$, such that on all of $U$
$$n=\partial_{x^0},\qquad g_{00}\equiv-1,\qquad g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}.$$

**(b) Cone domination.** The chart and radius in (a) can be chosen so every nonzero future causal vector at any point of $U$ satisfies
$$|v_s|\le K v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le K v^0\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad v^0\ge K^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$

**(c) Curve form.** Every future causal curve $\gamma:I\to U$ of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] has strictly increasing time coordinate, and for all $s<t$ in $I$
$$x^0(\gamma(s))<x^0(\gamma(t)),\qquad |x_s(\gamma(t))-x_s(\gamma(s))|\le K\left(x^0(\gamma(t))-x^0(\gamma(s))\right).$$
Consequently every spatial component satisfies the same bound, and the curve image is the graph of a $K$-Lipschitz function into Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ over the interval $x^0(\gamma(I))$.

**(d) Flat minorant cone.** The same chart can be chosen so the constant-coordinate metric $\eta_{16}=-(dx^0)^2+16\sum_i(dx^i)^2$ has every nonzero $\eta_{16}$-causal vector $g$-timelike throughout $U$. If $q,q'\in U$ and $\eta_{16}(x(q')-x(q),x(q')-x(q))<0$, then $q\ll q'$ if $x^0(q')>x^0(q)$, and $q'\ll q$ otherwise.

**(e) General temporal charts: exact compact uniformity.** For any chart $(U',z)$ define its temporal locus
$$P=\{q\in U':\nabla z^0(q)\text{ is past timelike}\}.$$
For every compact set $K_0\subset P$ there is $L\ge1$ such that all nonzero future causal vectors based in $K_0$, with coordinate components and Euclidean norm taken in $z$, satisfy
$$|v_s|\le L v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le L v^0,\qquad v^0\ge L^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$
In particular these bounds hold throughout any relatively compact $U_0\Subset U'$ whose closure is contained in $P$, equivalently whose time gradient is past timelike on its entire closure. Timelikeness merely on $U_0$ gives local bounds at each point and uniform bounds on each compact subset of $U_0$; it does not alone give a uniform bound on all of $U_0$.

No additional choice is used to select the pointwise linear bases or compact cone constants. Countable and Dependent Choice are explicitly required only for the general absolutely continuous curve clause (c), through its actual calculus suppliers.

after.claim: (Existence of admissible partitions.) The compact set $\alpha([a,b])$ is covered by finitely many strictly convex normal balls $C_1,\dots,C_m$ ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]), and the preimages $\alpha^{-1}(C_j)$ form an open cover of $[a,b]$ with Lebesgue number $\lambda>0$; any partition of mesh less than $\lambda$ has each subarc in some $C_j$, which we call $U_i^N$.

(The maximality inequality.) For every admissible partition, $L_g(\alpha)=\sum_iL_g(\alpha|_{[t_i,t_{i+1}]})\le\sum_id_{U_i^N}(\alpha(t_i),\alpha(t_{i+1}))$ by [L1]; hence $L_g(\alpha)\le\liminf_N\sum_id_{U_i^N}(\alpha(t_i),\alpha(t_{i+1}))$.

(The interpolating geodesic and its length.) For an admissible partition $\mathcal P_N$, let $\gamma_N:[a,b]\to M$ be the concatenation over $i$ of the radial geodesics $\gamma_{p_i,p_{i+1}}$ of $U_i^N$, affinely parametrized on $[t_i,t_{i+1}]$. By [L1] and [L2], $$\sum_id_{U_i^N}(p_i,p_{i+1})=\sum_iL_g(\gamma_{p_i,p_{i+1}})=L_g(\gamma_N).$$

(Uniform convergence of the interpolants.) Let $W$ be a compact coordinate neighborhood of $\alpha([a,b])$. On $W$ the maps $(p,q)\mapsto\exp_p^{-1}(q)$ and $q\mapsto q$ are uniformly continuous, and the maximal g-speed of the radial geodesics joining pairs of nearby points is bounded by a constant times their coordinate distance divided by $|t_{i+1}-t_i|$; consequently, as the mesh tends to zero both the displacement $p_{i+1}-p_i$ and the deviation of the radial geodesic from the subarc tend to zero uniformly: $\gamma_N\to\alpha$ uniformly on $[a,b]$. More precisely, for every $\varepsilon>0$, uniform continuity of $\exp^{-1}$ on the compact set of pairs $(p,q)\in W\times W$ with $d_h(p,q)\le\delta$ gives, for mesh small enough, that the radial geodesic of $v_i=\exp_{p_i}^{-1}(p_{i+1})$ stays in the $\varepsilon$-neighborhood of the subarc, because its endpoints are the endpoints of the subarc and $v_i$ is within $o(1)$ of the displacement $p_{i+1}-p_i$; the case of a single displacement is the mean value estimate for $q\mapsto\exp_p^{-1}(q)$ near the diagonal.

(Almost everywhere convergence of the speeds.) On the chart of [L3] around any point of $\alpha([a,b])$ write $v_i^N:=\exp_{p_i}^{-1}(p_{i+1})$ in coordinates and let $s_i^N:=t_{i+1}-t_i$. Since $\exp_p^{-1}(q)=\psi(q-p)+o(|q-p|)$ near the diagonal with $\psi$ the chart identification of the identity, $v_i^N=(\alpha(t_{i+1})-\alpha(t_i))+o(s_i^N)$ uniformly on the compact image. At every parameter $t$ that is a Lebesgue point of the integrable function $t\mapsto(x\circ\alpha)'(t)$ and not a partition point, the secant velocities $(x(\alpha(t_{i+1}))-x(\alpha(t_i)))/s_i^N$ over the intervals containing $t$ converge to $(x\circ\alpha)'(t)$, hence $v_i^N/s_i^N\to(x\circ\alpha)'(t)$; therefore the constant Lorentzian speed of the affine geodesic $\gamma_N$ on that interval, $d_{U_i^N}(p_i,p_{i+1})/s_i^N$, converges to $\sqrt{-g(\alpha'(t),\alpha'(t))}$ by [L7] and continuity of $g$ and the chart conversion. Since [L4] gives full measure for the set of such $t$, $f_N(t):=L_g$-speed of $\gamma_N$ at $t$ converges almost everywhere to $f(t):=\sqrt{-g(\alpha'(t),\alpha'(t))}$.

(Domination and Fatou.) Let $\psi_N(t):=(x^0(\alpha(t_{i+1}))-x^0(\alpha(t_i)))/s_i^N$ for $t\in[t_i,t_{i+1})$, the piecewise constant refinement ratio of $x^0\circ\alpha$. Then $\int_a^b\psi_N=\sum_i\Delta_ix^0=x^0(\alpha(b))-x^0(\alpha(a))$ is constant in $N$, and $\psi_N\to(x^0\circ\alpha)'$ almost everywhere by [L4]. By [L3], $f_N\le C\psi_N$ almost everywhere for a constant $C$ depending on the finitely many charts, and similarly $f\le C(x^0\circ\alpha)'$; the functions $C\psi_N-f_N\ge0$ satisfy $\int_a^b(C\psi_N-f_N)=C(x^0(\alpha(b))-x^0(\alpha(a)))-\sum_id_{U_i^N}$ and converge almost everywhere to $C(x^0\circ\alpha)'-f$. Fatou's lemma [L5] gives $$C\bigl(x^0(\alpha(b))-x^0(\alpha(a))\bigr)-L_g(\alpha)\le\liminf_N\Bigl(C\bigl(x^0(\alpha(b))-x^0(\alpha(a))\bigr)-\sum_id_{U_i^N}\Bigr),$$ that is, $\limsup_N\sum_id_{U_i^N}\le L_g(\alpha)$. Combined with step 2.1 this proves (a).

(Upper semicontinuity.) Let $\alpha_k\to\alpha$ uniformly and let $\varepsilon>0$. Choose finitely many strictly convex normal balls covering $\alpha([a,b])$ and a partition of mesh smaller than twice its Lebesgue number, refining if necessary so that each $\alpha([t_i,t_{i+1}])$ lies in one ball $U_i$ with room to spare, and such that by [L7] and uniform convergence also $\alpha_k([t_i,t_{i+1}])\subseteq U_i$ for all $k\ge k_0$ and all $i$. Then by [L1], $L_g(\alpha_k)=\sum_iL_g(\alpha_k|_{[t_i,t_{i+1}]})\le\sum_id_{U_i}(\alpha_k(t_i),\alpha_k(t_{i+1}))$; the right-hand side is a finite sum of continuous functions of the pair $(\alpha_k(t_i),\alpha_k(t_{i+1}))$ ([L2]), so $$\limsup_kL_g(\alpha_k)\le\sum_id_{U_i}\bigl(\alpha(t_i),\alpha(t_{i+1})\bigr).$$

(Passing to the limit in the partition.) The right-hand side is a refined sum along the partition for $\alpha$, so by part (a) it tends to $L_g(\alpha)$ as the mesh tends to zero, while the left-hand side does not depend on the partition. Hence $\limsup_kL_g(\alpha_k)\le L_g(\alpha)$, which is (b).
(Conclusion.) Part (a) is steps 1.1-4.1 and part (b) is steps 5.1 and 6.1.
